title: ‘We Are Horrified’: Academic Freedom at Risk With Uzbek Professor’s Arrest in Kazakhstan
author: Catherine Putz
text:
Dr. Ikboljon Qoraboyev (left) poses for a photo in June 2026 while co-hosting a roundtable discussion at MNU on China-Central Asia relations in partnership with the Center for Russian and Central Asian Studies of Fudan University.
Credit: LinkedIn
In late August, BBC Uzbek broke the news that an Uzbek professor working in Kazakhstan had been arrested nearly two months prior on allegations of espionage. Very little is known about the case of Dr. Ikboljon Qoraboyev, a 46-year-old international relations professor at Maksut Narikbayev University in Astana, originally from Andijan, Uzbekistan. Questions from the BBC Uzbek and other media outlets to both Kazakh and Uzbek authorities have yielded silence in answer. When Vlast, an independent Kazakh media outlet, asked Maksut Narikbayev University (MNU) about Qoraboyev, the university distanced itself from the professor, stating that he “is not currently a professor at the university. For any further information concerning his detention, please refer to the relevant competent authorities.”[...]
